data.title: Polish Monetary Policy Council Member Joanna Tyrowicz Says Rates Should Rise Sharply
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Polish media quoted Monetary Policy Council member Joanna Tyrowicz as saying that interest rates should rise sharply and that the council should clearly communicate a hawkish stance, including that rate increases are not a one-off measure and that the central bank is firmly committed to raising borrowing costs as needed.

Tyrowicz said that a year ago in the summer, when inflation was lower and its trend was improving, she considered interest rates of around 5% insufficient to bring inflation back to its target range. Rates are now lower, she said, while the inflation outlook is concerning.

Poland’s Monetary Policy Council kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75% earlier this month.

data.title: Barclays: Hawkish Fed Could Pressure Stocks; AI Slowdown and Sustained Rate Hikes Are Hard to Reconcile
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Barclays warned on November 20 that global stocks could remain under pressure through year-end if the Federal Reserve sends further hawkish signals or inflation data exceed market expectations. The bank said concern that the Fed may no longer support stock prices poses a bigger challenge than recent volatility in AI-related stocks.

Barclays strategist Emmanuel Cau and his team said strong economic growth and persistently high inflation had prompted a sharp repricing of rate expectations, tightening financial conditions, strengthening the dollar, reducing excess market liquidity and weighing on equity valuations. The bank compared the current environment with December 2018, when stocks fell about 20% before rebounding strongly in early 2019 after the Fed turned dovish.

Markets have fully priced in a Fed rate hike in December, and recent comments by Fed Governor Christopher Waller prompted speculation about a 50-basis-point increase. Barclays economists disagreed, saying a hike of that size would send a panic signal and imply that the Fed had made a mistake by pausing rate increases in October. Markets expect about three rate hikes over the coming year, but Barclays said that outlook conflicts with recent stock-market performance. If the selloff reflects concern that the AI investment cycle is fading, slower AI investment would ultimately weigh on growth, ease overheating pressures and reduce the need for further monetary tightening. Barclays said a marked slowdown in AI investment and a persistently hawkish Fed stance are difficult to sustain together over the long term.

Barclays said financial markets increasingly show late-cycle characteristics, while market performance has diverged somewhat from economic fundamentals. U.S. retail sales and Germany’s ZEW economic sentiment index both exceeded expectations, and corporate earnings continued to grow. Nvidia’s latest results, the bank said, supported the view that the AI capital-spending cycle remains solid. Barclays reiterated that enthusiasm for AI may have peaked, but the investment race is far from over; a late-cycle economy does not mean the expansion is about to end, and recent risk aversion and selling may have gone too far. It said the Fed’s December rate decision and subsequent CPI data will be key to risk appetite, and stocks could remain under pressure through year-end if inflation exceeds expectations or the Fed turns more hawkish.

data.title: South Africa’s Richards Bay Terminal Loads Record Chrome Cargo on Largest Carrier to Visit
data.description: According to Bloomberg, South Africa’s Richards Bay Bulk Terminal loaded a record chrome cargo aboard the largest bulk carrier to call at the facility. The loading was a bright spot in logistics performance as Durban, the country’s biggest port, continues to underperform.

data.title: China Buyers Cancel Palm Oil Cargoes as Storage Space Runs Short
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Chinese buyers have canceled several palm oil cargoes as the country’s inventories hover near a five-year high and storage space runs short. The cancellations add pressure to a market already dealing with excess Malaysian supply.

data.title: XMR1 Falls 99.8% From About $500 to $0.90 After Selloff
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Ember Monitoring, an XMR1 deployment wallet transferred 5.2 million tokens to an address. Some of the tokens were subsequently sold, and XMR1’s price fell about 99.8%, from approximately $500 to $0.90.

data.title: Polygon Releases Heimdall v0.14.0 as Purley Hard Fork Activates on Mainnet and Amoy Testnet
data.description:
Polygon has released Heimdall v0.14.0 for mainnet and the Amoy testnet, where the Purley hard fork was activated simultaneously. According to Foresight News, the public release matches the features of the previously distributed v0.14.0-priv version, and its source code has also been made public.

The Purley updates require validator vote extensions to be signed and certified in every block that contains them, and cross-chain bridge events to be confirmed before execution. Staking updates are accepted only at a validator’s next nonce. Expired checkpoint buffers are retained until replaced by newly approved checkpoints, while canceled governance proposals without a target address are no longer charged fees.

data.title: STOCKS | US Futures Decline as AI-Related Selling Reaches Asia and Europe
data.description: According to Bloomberg, US equity futures fell on Friday as Wall Street’s overnight selloff spread to Asia and Europe. Anthropic PBC’s stock-market debut failed to ease concerns around the AI trade.

data.title: Lufthansa to Cut 1,000 Jobs at Unprofitable Mainline Airline
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Deutsche Lufthansa AG will eliminate 1,000 jobs at its namesake airline to turn around the unprofitable mainline unit, as high fuel costs pressure Europe’s largest aviation group.

data.title: AI TRENDS | CITIC Securities, CICC and Others Invest in DeepSeek
data.description:
Hangzhou Chengyan Enterprise Management Consulting Partnership (Limited Partnership) became a DeepSeek shareholder for the first time on November 17, ranking as its third-largest shareholder. According to Odaily, several brokerages, including CITIC Securities, China International Capital Corporation, China Securities and Shenwan Hongyuan, contributed funds to Hangzhou Chengyan. With the new shareholder, Liang Wenfeng’s direct stake declined, but he remained DeepSeek’s second-largest direct shareholder.

Zhang Kaifeng, a non-bank analyst at Orient Securities, said brokerages with reserves of high-quality industrial projects have greater potential on the asset side. Traditional brokerage businesses are more affected by market trading, the pace of investment banking issuance and equity-market volatility. The listing of high-quality, privately held equity projects can make the value of alternative investments, private equity funds and industrial funds more visible.

data.title: Japan’s 89.5-Hour Stock Market Closure Puts Kioxia and On-Chain Traders in Focus
data.description: Japan’s stock market is set to close after trading on November 20 for a three-day holiday, leaving the Tokyo spot market shut for 89.5 hours, from 14:30 UTC+8 on Friday until 08:00 UTC+8 the following Tuesday. According to BlockBeats On-chain Detection, on-chain Japanese stock perpetual contracts will continue trading during the closure. The headline points to intensified positioning among large on-chain traders after Kioxia’s sharp decline and raises the question of how much of the premium-driven gains seen during a September holiday held after Tokyo reopened; it does not provide details on those outcomes or current positions.

data.title: Anthropic to Replace Strategy (MSTR) in Indexes at Month-End, Potentially Affecting Bitcoin Buying
data.description: At the U.S. market close on November 30, global index funds are set to add newly listed Anthropic (ANT) and remove Strategy (MSTR), which holds about 850,800 bitcoin. According to BlockBeats On-chain Detection, Anthropic is set to enter the indexes on its seventh trading day, prompting passive purchases of ANT and sales of MSTR. The index changes could also indirectly affect bitcoin buying through Strategy.

data.title: SanDisk Stock Split Settlement Leaves 1,757 Addresses With $9.74 Million in Losses, Two Whales Down $2.49 Million
data.description:
A SanDisk stock split prompted Trade.xyz to settle legacy SNDK perpetual positions on Hyperliquid, leaving 1,757 addresses with combined losses of about $9.74 million. According to BlockBeats On-chain Detection, the contracts were settled at $755.16, SanDisk’s U.S. stock closing price before the split; four addresses each lost more than $500,000, and all held long positions.

The largest loss was recorded by address 0xea00, which had held 1,750 SNDK contracts since October 22 and added to its position around $1,388. Its 2,500 contracts were settled at $755.16, 43.6% below the average entry price of $1,338.81, resulting in a realized loss of $1.4591 million. Address 0x519c lost $1.0283 million on 2,610.9 contracts entered at an average of $1,149. Together, the two addresses lost nearly $2.49 million. Two other addresses, 0x0f85 and 0xf929, lost $823,900 and $731,000, respectively.

Unlike holders of SanDisk shares, who received eight shares for each share in the split and could continue holding them, Trade.xyz required pre-split contracts to be closed and settled. The unrealized losses on the positions therefore became realized, and the traders would need to open new positions at post-split prices to remain long. None of the four addresses had traded SNDK again as of publication. The SNDK perpetual contract’s mark price on Trade.xyz was $91.70; compared with the split-adjusted benchmark of $98.13, its 24-hour decline was 6.51%.

data.title: Honda Recalls 16,387 U.S. Vehicles Over Engine-Stalling Risk
data.description: According to Jin10, Honda is recalling 16,387 vehicles in the United States because engines stalling while driving could increase the risk of a crash or injury.

data.title: ICBA Calls for Delay in Stablecoin Cash-Equivalent Accounting Proposal
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, the Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA) wrote to the Financial Accounting Standards Board on November 19, urging it not to finalize a proposal to include some digital assets in cash-equivalent assessments. The association called for waiting until the GENIUS Act and related regulations are implemented and the market develops before deciding whether to amend U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.

ICBA said the proposal could create additional disclosure, audit, and compliance requirements for community banks that do not hold digital assets. It also argued that the broad term “certain digital assets” could bring tokenized bank deposits under an accounting framework intended for payment stablecoins, and called for a clear distinction between bank deposits and payment stablecoins, with disclosure requirements limited to relevant information needs.

ICBA estimated that widespread stablecoin adoption could lead to more than $1 trillion in community bank deposit outflows and reduce community bank lending by $850 billion.

data.title: France's Financial Sector Advisory Committee Urges EU to Tighten Crypto Ad Rules
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, France's Financial Sector Advisory Committee has recommended that the EU strictly regulate advertising for high-risk crypto assets targeting retail investors. It also called for stronger risk disclosures for lending and staking services.

data.description: According to Jin10, France's INSEE business confidence index stood at 95 in November, compared with expectations of 96 and a previous reading of 97.

data.title: STOCKS | Analyst Sees Opportunity as Technology Stock Valuations Plunge
data.description:
Technology stocks, particularly AI-related shares, have suffered sharp valuation declines, prompting debate over whether pessimism has been fully priced in. According to Odaily, the Nasdaq 100, S&P 500 Information Technology Index and Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index are at multiyear lows on forward earnings valuations. Semiconductor companies and other AI infrastructure providers have been hit hardest, while companies that have invested heavily in data centers have also been affected.

Signs of further capitulation selling emerged this week, making it difficult to time an entry. Still, some investors see opportunity, citing strong earnings from Nvidia, Anthropic’s high-profile debut and reduced positioning in the technology sector.

Louis Navellier, founder of Navellier & Associates Inc., said he expects a strong rebound in AI stocks, noting that corporate earnings remain strong while valuations are unusually low. He said shares of Micron Technology and Super Micro Computer are trading at less than four times expected earnings, calling them a strong buying opportunity.

Johan Van der Biest, global co-head of equity management at Candriam, said recent earnings results indicate cloud services and AI computing demand remain strong despite uncertainty. He said technology stocks could continue to outperform the broader market.

data.title: UBS Raises Palo Alto Networks Price Target to $400, Says Growth Supports Valuation Premium
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, UBS raised its price target for Palo Alto Networks to $400 from $390 and maintained its Neutral rating, saying accelerating business growth supports the company’s valuation premium.

In the company’s first fiscal quarter, net new annual recurring revenue (ARR) exceeded guidance by $180 million. Next-generation security ARR rose 66% year over year, or about 37% on a pro forma basis, while total revenue increased 39%, or about 23% on a pro forma basis. UBS said the metrics accelerated significantly from the previous quarter.

Observability revenue grew to about four times its year-earlier level and contributed roughly 25% of net new ARR. Organic growth in product revenue also accelerated. Palo Alto Networks has posted faster organic growth for three consecutive quarters, and UBS expects pro forma revenue growth of at least 16% through the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027.

UBS said customers are consolidating cybersecurity providers, giving large, integrated platforms a larger share of new cybersecurity spending. It added that Palo Alto Networks’ acquisition of AI startup Applied Compute opens up new growth opportunities but increases the complexity of business development and integration.

The stock is valued at 44 times UBS’s forecast for Palo Alto Networks’ 2028 calendar-year free cash flow. UBS said the premium is reasonable given the company’s sustained growth acceleration.
